title: Leaks Suggest Galaxy S27 Pro, Ultra Get Horizontal Camera Bar
excerpt: Reported case listings and CAD renders tip a wider camera bar, built-in Qi2 magnets and larger batteries for Samsung's Pro and Ultra models — none of it confirmed by Samsung
body:
• Leaked case listings and CAD renders suggest Samsung's Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra could switch to a wide horizontal camera bar, replacing years of vertical camera layouts — Samsung has confirmed nothing.
  • Reports tip larger silicon-carbon batteries of about 5,200mAh for the Pro and about 5,700mAh for the Ultra, up from the 5,000mAh ceiling on recent Ultra models.
  • The redesign is reported to free internal space for built-in Qi2 magnets, so magnetic accessories could attach without a special case.
  • The S27 series is reported to be unveiled in January or February 2027, with final Pro and Ultra hardware still undecided, according to the reports.

Samsung's next flagship phones are still months away, but a series of reported leaks now points to a clear design change at the top of the range. Leaked case listings and CAD-based renders suggest the Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra could adopt a large horizontal camera bar across the top of the back, while the standard Galaxy S27 and S27+ reportedly keep a vertical camera layout. Samsung has not announced the phones, their specifications or a launch date, and every detail in this report should be read as unconfirmed leak reporting, as set out by Android Headlines and other outlets covering the leaks.

What the case leaks and renders show

Android Headlines reported that SammyGuru spotted around 40 case renders for the two phones across several e-commerce sites, and that they all pointed to the same design: a large rectangular camera bar stretching across the top of the back. The site described it as a big departure from the vertically stacked cameras Samsung has used for years, and closer to Apple's iPhone 17 Pro design.

Separate reporting summarised by HindFirst made the same split within the range: leaked case images suggested the S27 and S27+ may retain a vertical cutout similar to the current design, while the Pro and Ultra camera module could be much wider, spanning nearly the entire width of the back. Android Headlines also reported the Pro is expected to be a smaller Ultra without the S Pen, with a display around 6.6 inches, and that the Pro and Ultra reportedly share nearly identical designs, making it hard to tell which leaked case belongs to which phone.

Why the bar might be about magnets and battery

The reported reason for the redesign goes beyond appearance. Both Android Headlines and HindFirst reported a theory that moving the cameras into a horizontal bar could free internal space for built-in Qi2 magnets. That would let the Pro and Ultra snap onto magnetic accessories and chargers without needing a special case. Android Headlines noted the lack of built-in magnets has been one of the biggest complaints about Samsung flagships, and that the base S27 and S27+ reportedly retain the familiar design and likely skip the built-in magnets.

The same reports tip larger batteries for the higher-end models. HindFirst reported silicon-carbon batteries of approximately 5,200mAh for the Pro and around 5,700mAh for the Ultra, while stressing final specifications will only be confirmed after an official Samsung announcement. Android Headlines reported a recent leak pointing to a roughly 5,700mAh cell in the S27 Ultra, which would break Samsung's 5,000mAh ceiling. Reporting covered by TechTimes, pointed to a rated capacity of 5,534mAh in a 3C filing translating to an advertised 5,700mAh, and to a three-camera setup in the CAD renders — a 200MP main sensor, a 50MP ultrawide and a 50MP 5x periscope telephoto, with the dedicated 3x telephoto reportedly dropped.

Displays, memory and a possible price rise — all reported, none confirmed

HindFirst reported the Pro and Ultra are also expected to feature Samsung's new M16 OLED display technology, while the S27 and S27+ are rumoured to use M14 OLED panels. It said Samsung is still finalising storage and RAM decisions, with UFS 5.0 storage and LPDDR6 memory under consideration, and suggested those high-end components could lead to a price increase for the Pro and Ultra models. No pricing has been confirmed by Samsung, and readers should treat any price figures circulating in leak coverage as speculation until an official announcement.

What happens next

HindFirst reported that development of the Galaxy S27 and S27+ is reportedly nearing completion, while final hardware decisions for the Pro and Ultra are still pending, which is why Samsung has not yet set a launch date. It said the series could be unveiled in January or February 2027. Android Headlines put the expected launch in early 2027, likely around February, and expected plenty more leaks before then. Until Samsung confirms the lineup at an official launch, the horizontal camera bar, the larger batteries and the built-in magnets remain reported plans drawn from cases and renders — not finished products.
